mean: to lose everything, gains and all

mean: ominous, an unlucky thing to say
lit: not even a matter of omens: so ill-starred it should not be said at all

story.text: Engi began as a Buddhist term, the rendering of the Sanskrit pratītyasamutpāda: the teaching that all things arise in dependence on causes and conditions. In Japan the word came to mean the founding story of a temple or shrine, and later a sign of what is to come. Engi ga ii is a good omen; engi de mo nai rejects a remark as so ill-omened it should not be spoken.
story.source: Buddhist term 縁起 (Sanskrit pratītyasamutpāda, dependent origination)

ctx.en: After the earthquake, getting people out from under the rubble was a race against time.
